text.arabic_uthmani: لَوْ نَشَآءُ جَعَلْنَٰهُ أُجَاجًۭا فَلَوْلَا تَشْكُرُونَ

words.gloss_range: counterfactual conditional particle opening an unrealized capacity frame

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the imperfect verb governed by the opening condition
the later echoing particle with shifted exhortative force

words.prose: {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}) opens the ayah as a counterfactual condition, not as an optative wish or a loose possibility. Because it governs {{ar:نَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:nashāʾu}}), the first beat presents divine capacity as withheld but still active: the water is drinkable by restraint, not by lack of power to alter it. Its initial position makes the whole line unfold as staged architecture: condition, hypothetical transformation, then reproach. The later {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) reuses the opening sound with a changed function, so the final demand for gratitude audibly answers the first counterfactual.

topics.headline: counterfactual restraint opens the ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse begins from divine power deliberately not exercised, so drinkable water appears as restrained capacity rather than ordinary permanence.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}) as the particle introducing the counterfactual protasis, and the following imperfect keeps capacity current rather than closing it into a past hypothetical.

topics.headline: condition launches a three-beat frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening particle makes the ayah process as condition, result, and reproach rather than as a flat statement about water.
topics.reason: The clause analysis marks {{ar:لَوْ نَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:law nashāʾu}}) as protasis, {{ar:جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجًا}} ({{tr:jaʿalnāhu ujājan}}) as apodosis, and {{ar:فَلَوْلَا تَشْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:falawlā tashkurūna}}) as the consequence.

topics.headline: opening sound returns as reproach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same particle sound returning near the end with a changed job, linking unrealized threat to demanded gratitude.
topics.reason: {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}) stands separately at the opening, while the later {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) shares its sound but functions as exhortative reproach.

words.gloss_range: divine willing in an imperfect counterfactual protasis, with the object of willing left compressed
words.root_gloss_range: willing, desiring, choosing, determining; disputed root-family links to thinghood are only a qualified pressure here

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the making verb that realizes the hypothetical result

words.prose: {{ar:نَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:nashāʾu}}) is the first content verb after the particle, so the threat begins in divine willing before it reaches the water. Its imperfect form under {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}) keeps the capacity current and repeatable, while the absence of an expressed object compresses the volition: what is willed is supplied by the following making clause. The root range gives the verb determination and selection, not a passing preference. A disputed root-family link with thinghood may color the idea that state-realization begins with will, but the local grammar keeps the selected sense as willing that leads to rendering. Its pairing with {{ar:جَعَلْنَاهُ}} ({{tr:jaʿalnāhu}}) also places water inside a repeated provision-threat pattern, including the crop warning earlier in the surah (56:65) and the water challenge elsewhere (67:30).

topics.headline: imperfect willing keeps capacity current
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the threat is not a closed past hypothetical; the imperfect keeps divine capacity live in the moment of address.
topics.reason: QAC and verb-instance evidence identify {{ar:نَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:nashāʾu}}) as an imperfect indicative governed by the counterfactual protasis, with no expressed volitional object.

topics.headline: will is determination, not bare preference
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the threatened bitter state is grounded first in sovereign determination, while disputed thinghood-etymology remains only a qualified pressure.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows' determination sense is coherent locally, but the disputed link between willing and thinghood cannot govern the parse because the local verb is simply divine willing in a conditional frame.

topics.headline: first-person agency is fused into the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine speaker is grammatically present inside the verb without a separate pronoun, keeping the short protasis concentrated on will.
topics.reason: The verb carries first-person plural agreement, and the finite form makes volition act inside the conditional rather than naming it as an abstract noun.

topics.headline: will hands off to making across provision threats
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that willing and making form a repeated provision-threat sequence, so the water line parallels other survival domains rather than standing alone.
topics.reason: The local syntax pairs {{ar:نَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:nashāʾu}}) with {{ar:جَعَلْنَاهُ}} ({{tr:jaʿalnāhu}}), and CRITICAL inter-ayah rows identify provision-threat parallels at 56:65 and 67:30.

words.gloss_range: rendered it into a state; here a transformative double-object construction over prior water
words.root_gloss_range: making, rendering, assigning, creating, appointing, and unrelated nominal branches; local grammar selects rendering an existing referent into a quality
words.prose: {{ar:جَعَلْنَاهُ}} ({{tr:jaʿalnāhu}}) converts the prior act of willing into an imposed water-state. The attached -hu suffix resumes the water already under discussion, and {{ar:أُجَاجًا}} ({{tr:ujājan}}) supplies the second complement, so the grammar is not creation of a new object but rendering existing water into a hostile quality. The perfect form makes that unrealized result feel complete the moment divine will applies, and the answer arrives without an emphatic la- prefix, leaving the compact perfect verb itself to carry the threat. Broader {{ar:ج ع ل}} ({{tr:j-ʿ-l}}) branches such as creating, appointing, or fabricating are narrowed by the pronoun-plus-quality construction: the active branch here is controlled transformation. The word also links this water threat to other provision scenes, including the crop threat at 56:65, the sweet-salt water field at 25:53, and the later same-surah inversion where human making turns provision into denial (56:82).

topics.headline: pronoun and result complement make transformation explicit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the water is the affected patient and bitter-brackishness is the imposed result, so the threat targets the quality of an existing provision.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the suffix as first object and {{ar:أُجَاجًا}} ({{tr:ujājan}}) as second object, with the suffix resuming the water under discussion.

topics.headline: making narrows to property assignment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that {{ar:جَعَلْنَاهُ}} ({{tr:jaʿalnāhu}}) means rendering the water into a state here, not creating it from nothing or fabricating it.
topics.reason: V4 includes a broad making/creating branch and a state-rendering branch, but the local double-object construction with a quality complement selects state-rendering.

topics.headline: unprefixed perfect apodosis makes the threat swift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the counterfactual answer arrives as a compact, unprefixed perfect verb, so the threatened result is grammatically complete rather than gradual.
topics.reason: The word is tagged as perfect in the apodosis, and the CRITICAL rows note the direct unprefixed surface compared with the parallel at 56:65.

topics.headline: making language joins water and provision fields
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same making root connects water-quality control, crop vulnerability, and human misuse of provision across nearby and related passages.
topics.reason: CRITICAL inter-ayah rows give concrete links to 25:53, 56:65, 56:82, and 56:73; these are kept as echoes without making them control the local parse.

words.gloss_range: bitter-brackish, burningly saline water-quality adjective in the result slot
words.root_gloss_range: blazing, burning, crackling intensity and water-specific salty/brackish harshness; local use selects the water-quality adjective

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the verb assigning this resultant quality

words.prose: {{ar:أُجَاجًا}} ({{tr:ujājan}}) names the exact state the water would be made to bear. Its accusative qualitative form is the second object of {{ar:جَعَلْنَاهُ}} ({{tr:jaʿalnāhu}}), so the word is not a free description but the imposed result. Semantically it is narrower than generic bitterness: the water becomes brackish, salty, and burning to use, with the root's fire-pressure making water feel hostile rather than refreshing. The repeated jīm sound gives that burning-brackish harshness an audible bite at the point where the threat lands. The indefinite adjective form also matters because this rare root appears here as a predicable quality, not merely as a named water category. Its Quranic field belongs to sweet-salt water contrasts, including 25:53 and 35:12, but 56:70 compresses that binary into one threatened transformation of the same water.

topics.headline: the adjective is the imposed result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word supplies the water's resultant condition inside the making construction, not an independent descriptive afterthought.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:أُجَاجًا}} ({{tr:ujājan}}) the accusative second object of {{ar:جَعَلْنَاهُ}} ({{tr:jaʿalnāhu}}), and the local form is an indefinite qualitative adjective.

topics.headline: brackish water carries burning force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the threat is not simply bad taste but water made actively hostile to drinking through burning salinity.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL lexical rows consistently tie the local word to water-specific salty or brackish harshness and to the root-family fire image; V4 has no root rows to contradict this.

topics.headline: rare root belongs to water-quality contrasts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that {{ar:أُجَاجًا}} ({{tr:ujājan}}) belongs to a specialized water-quality field, so the ayah threatens loss of drinkability rather than using a generic adjective.
topics.reason: The contextual profile marks the root as low occurrence, and the CRITICAL rows cite the other water-quality passages at 25:53 and 35:12.

topics.headline: doubled sound matches the harsh quality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the doubled consonantal pressure makes the harsh, burning quality audible at the point where the threat lands.
topics.reason: The word's root shape repeats the central consonant, and the CRITICAL phonetic rows connect that texture to the burning-brackish sense.

words.gloss_range: consequential conjunction fused to the following exhortative particle

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the reproach clause governed by the conjunction

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge where the completed bitter-water threat becomes a reason for direct reproach. It does not merely mean a loose and; it scopes over the whole {{ar:لَوْلَا تَشْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:lawlā tashkurūna}}) clause, turning withheld harm into the immediate ground for gratitude. As a single-letter proclitic fused in {{ar:فَلَوْلَا}} ({{tr:falawlā}}), it makes consequence inseparable from the exhortation. The particle also keeps relation and separation at once: first the counterfactual result is complete, then the demand follows from it, and the reproach frame points forward to the next provision challenge at 56:71.

topics.headline: the threat becomes the reason for gratitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that gratitude is demanded as the direct consequence of withheld bittering, not as an unrelated moral add-on.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks {{ar:فَلَوْلَا تَشْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:falawlā tashkurūna}}) as the result clause, and the CRITICAL rows identify the particle as causal/resultative.

topics.headline: one-letter consequence fuses to exhortation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the written and recited fusion makes the reproach sound like the immediate continuation of the counterfactual.
topics.reason: The conjunction is a proclitic attached to {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}), so the consequence relation and reproach particle are heard together.

topics.headline: the reproach hands forward to the next challenge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reproach closes the water proof while setting up the next concrete provision question at 56:71.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL boundary row names 56:71 as the next interrogative challenge, so the forward bridge is kept as discourse continuity rather than as a new lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: hortatory reproach particle governing the following imperfect, not a nominal counterfactual

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the imperfect verb targeted by the exhortation
the opening counterfactual particle echoed with changed force

words.prose: {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) turns the line from conditional demonstration into direct exhortative reproach. Its scope is local: it governs {{ar:تَشْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:tashkurūna}}), not the whole earlier counterfactual, and the following imperfect blocks the nominal sense of were it not for. The particle therefore keeps urging and blame together: it demands gratitude while marking its absence as culpable. Its compound shape echoes the opening {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}) but changes the function from unrealized condition to moral demand, and it sets up the final long verb ending as the audible landing of the reproach.

topics.headline: following imperfect selects exhortation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle asks why gratitude is not happening, rather than reopening a were-it-not-for condition.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:تَشْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:tashkurūna}}) the complement of {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}), and the following imperfect selects taḥḍīḍ rather than a nominal counterfactual reading.

topics.headline: urging and blame remain live together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final clause is not neutral information; it presses the addressees while blaming the missing response.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL semantic rows preserve both exhortation and reproach, and the clause profile marks the final unit as an exhortative consequence.

topics.headline: law sound returns with changed force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form recalls the opening condition while changing its function into reproach, making the ayah's sound pattern carry the argument.
topics.reason: {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) visibly contains the earlier sound but does not function as the same particle or as simple negation.

topics.headline: open vowels lead into the final demand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle leads acoustically into the long closing of the gratitude verb, making the demand prominent at the end.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL phonetic row ties the open particle to the final verb cadence without changing the grammatical analysis.

words.gloss_range: you give thanks, as an ongoing second-person plural action demanded by reproach
words.root_gloss_range: recognizing and praising a benefit, with root-family abundance and yielding imagery that colors but does not replace the local gratitude sense

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the hortatory particle giving the indicative verb reproach force

words.prose: {{ar:تَشْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:tashkurūna}}) is the ayah's final landing: after divine willing and making, the address turns to what the listeners are not doing. The imperfect makes the failure ongoing, and {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) gives the indicative verb its exhortative force, so this is not a bare imperative or a past complaint. The initial t- and the plural -ūna ending together make the addressees responsible without adding a separate pronoun. Its object is not stated, which keeps gratitude broad while the water argument supplies the concrete benefit. The root's active acknowledgment of benefit is primary; abundance images from the root family, including yielding much from little and intense rain, color gratitude as a return that should rise from provision, while the local sense remains thanking. Closure position makes gratitude, not bitter water, the final heard demand, and the final nasal nūn lets the unanswered response linger as the provision sequence moves to the next question at 56:71.

topics.headline: imperfect gratitude is an ongoing failure under reproach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final verb reproaches a continuing failure to thank, not one missed past act and not a simple command form.
topics.reason: The verb is imperfect indicative and is governed by hortatory {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}), which supplies the directive reproach force.

topics.headline: the ending makes the audience responsible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse-person shift: first-person divine capacity turns into second-person human obligation at the final word.
topics.reason: The morphology carries second-person masculine plural agreement, while earlier main verbs in the ayah carry first-person plural divine agency.

topics.headline: unstated object keeps concrete provision in view
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that gratitude is an active acknowledgment of received provision, with the object left compressed but recoverable from the water argument.
topics.reason: The verb instance marks no expressed object, the contextual valency profile shows this root-form often used absolutely, and V4 supports the benefit-recognition branch as the local sense.

topics.headline: abundance imagery colors but does not replace thanks
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that root-family images of abundant yielding and intense rain make gratitude feel like an abundant return from provision, while the local verb still means thanking.
topics.reason: V4 distinguishes the primary gratitude branch from animal, plant, and turbulence branches; the CRITICAL imagery can color the water context but cannot replace the local thanking sense.

topics.headline: gratitude is the final landing and next response frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends on the demanded human response and then carries that response frame into the next provision question at 56:71.
topics.reason: The final word is the gratitude verb, and the CRITICAL boundary row explicitly connects this closure to the next concrete provision question at 56:71.

1. **Will could transform drinkability into intense salinity.** In `نشاء`, `ش ي ء` **B001** again uses its accepted **“willing”** variant; `ج ع ل` **B002** supplies transformation; `ء ج ج` **B003** supplies bitter, intensely salty water. **Abductive move:** I infer that preserving fresh water is an ongoing non-transformation, not a property recipients secure. **Reading change:** freshness appears as contingent favor.

2. **Recognition should register the benefactor in the effect.** `ش ك ر` **B001** supplies recognizing a favor and praising its giver; **B002** supplies being sustained by little and showing its effect. **Abductive move:** I infer that potable water’s bodily effect should become visible as acknowledgment. **Reading change:** gratitude is evidential recognition of maintained usability.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Food, water, and fire arrive through multi-stage transformations that humans initiate or use locally but cannot secure at the level of growth, descent, or latent energy.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Debt, famine, cloud husbandry, minimal-input flourishing, tinder, and traveler supplies expose the operational dependencies inside ordinary provision.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Cloud delivery can become drink or brine
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Water is gathered in cloud, sent downward for drinking, and remains subject to conversion into bitter salinity; gratitude answers the contingency of the chain.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin baskın açıklaması bir varlığı belirli bir ad veya nitelikle anma ve onun öyle olduğunu söylemedir. Bununla birlikte aynı ifadenin bir başka yorumda o varlığı gerçekten söz konusu duruma getirme diye açıklandığı da kaydedilir; bu yüzden dal ancak bu yorum ayrılığı belirtilerek korunabilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek adlandırma ve söylemedir; aynı söz dizimine ilişkin durum değiştirme yorumu ayrı bir kaynak değişkesi olarak tutulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Kullanımın yalın olup olmadığı mekanik olarak çözümlenmemiştir; tanım bağımsız bir yalın anlam varsaymaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir varlığı belirli bir ad veya nitelikle anmak ya da onun öyle olduğunu söylemektir; aynı ifadenin bir yorumunda ise varlığı gerçekten o duruma getirme anlamı vardır.

facets.statement: Bir varlığı belli bir adla veya nitelikle anmayı ve onun öyle olduğunu söylemeyi bildirir.
Aynı tanıklık için, varlığı söylenen duruma gerçekten getirme biçiminde rakip bir yorum da aktarılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu tanıklık adlandırma ve söyleme açıklamasını verirken, aynı ifadenin durum değiştirme diye yorumlandığını da kaynak adı yüklemeden kaydeder.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir kişiye yapacağı iş veya yerine getireceği görev karşılığında ayrılan ücret, ödeme ya da armağanı açıkça tanımlar. İnsanların bir sefer veya önemli iş için aralarında kararlaştırdıkları ortak ödemeler de aynı karşılık belirleme çekirdeğine bağlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin yapacağı iş veya görev karşılığında ona verilmek üzere belirlenen ücret, ödeme ya da armağandır. Bir topluluğun sefer veya önemli bir iş için aralarında kararlaştırdığı ödemeler de bu çekirdeğin özel bir gerçekleşmesidir.

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.
